# Analysis

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

##install.packages("fivethirtyeight")
library(fivethirtyeight)

candy <- fivethirtyeight::candy_rankings

candy <- candy |>
  mutate(type = case_when(
    chocolate & fruity ~ "both",
    chocolate ~ "chocolate",
    fruity ~ "fruity",
    .default = "other"
  ))#creates a new column

#count(candy, type)
```

## Row 2

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
#| echo: false
#| height: 450px

# Calculate the correlation coefficient (r)
r_value <- round(cor(candy$sugarpercent, candy$winpercent, use = "complete.obs"), 2)

# Creating a tooltip for the scatter plot and the linear line
scatter_tooltip <- paste0(
  "<b>", candy$competitorname, "</b>",
  "<br>Sugar Percentile: ", round(candy$sugarpercent, 2),
  "<br>Win Percentage: ", round(candy$winpercent, 1), "%"
)
line_tooltip <- paste0("Linear Trend Line<br>Correlation (r): ", r_value)

# Sugar level (x), Popularity (y) scatter plot
sugar_pop <- ggplot(candy, aes(sugarpercent, winpercent)) +
  geom_point(aes(text = scatter_tooltip)) +
  geom_smooth(aes(text = line_tooltip), method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#89C0AE") +
  labs(
    title = "Sugar Content vs Popularity",
    subtitle = "Does more sugar mean more popular?",
    x = "Sugar percentile compared to other candies",
    y = "Percentage of matchups the candy won"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

ggplotly(sugar_pop, tooltip = "text")
```

# Data Table

This candy dataset includes 85 different candies and 14 different candy properties. The **Sugar Percentile** and **Price Percentile** columns represent percentile rankings, indicating how a candy's sugar content and price compare relative to all other candies in the dataset. For example, a sugar percentile of 0.85 means that particular candy has more sugar than 85% of the other candies in the dataset. The **Win Percentage** is scaled from 0-100 representing how often that candy won head-to-head matchups in the survey.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
table_data <- candy |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Candy Name"         = competitorname,
    "Chocolate"          = chocolate,
    "Fruity"             = fruity,
    "Caramel"            = caramel,
    "Peanuty/Almondy"    = peanutyalmondy,
    "Nougat"             = nougat,
    "Crisped Rice Wafer" = crispedricewafer,
    "Hard"               = hard,
    "Bar"                = bar,
    "Many per Package"   = pluribus,
    "Sugar Percentile"   = sugarpercent,
    "Price Percentile"   = pricepercent,
    "Win Percentage"     = winpercent,
    "Type"               = type
  )
knitr::kable(table_data)
```
